#1824. JJ Gabriel has set himself a huge target at Real Madrid

Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has revealed his ambition to win the Ballon d'Or as he moves closer to joining Real Madrid.

The 16-year-old gave an interview to Spanish newspaper Marca while training individually in Madrid, having not returned to United since requesting to leave the club in September.

Gabriel was presented with a front page of the newspaper featuring himself and responded: "Can I keep it?"

The forward was also asked why he preferred Real Madrid to Barcelona, with the teenager making his choice clear by replying: "Obviously, Madrid."

He then outlined his biggest ambition in football, saying: "My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or."

Gabriel is understood to have reached a verbal agreement with Real Madrid, who are hoping to complete the move in January. The Spanish club are planning for him to develop with their reserve side, Castilla, before potentially progressing into the first team.

The teenager has already spent time training in Barcelona before moving to the Spanish capital, where his representative Ali Barat is handling negotiations and helping arrange accommodation for Gabriel and his family.

His Irish passport is expected to make a move to Spain possible under FIFA regulations allowing certain players aged 16 to 18 to transfer within the European Union. However, Gabriel remains registered with United, meaning he cannot yet represent another club.

United are disappointed to lose one of their highly-rated academy prospects and had attempted to persuade him to stay by offering a new contract and a pathway towards senior football.

The club could receive training compensation if the transfer is completed, with reports suggesting the figure could be around £350,000.

Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut and was named Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season last term.

#1823. Thomas Tuchel defends ‘standout’ Arsenal star after England fan criticism

Thomas Tuchel has urged England supporters to stop booing Ben White and insists he has been a ‘standout’ player for Arsenal.

White made himself unavailable for England selection during Gareth Southgate’s reign after he left the squad during the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

It is understood that White was involved in a bust-up with Southgate’s assistant Steve Holland during England’s World Cup campaign shortly before leaving the squad.

In March this year, White made his first appearance for England in four years as he came off the bench to score the opening goal in the 1-1 draw with Uruguay at Wembley.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

However, White was booed by a section of England supporters at Wembley for his decision to make himself unavailable for the Three Lions.

‘We were not happy about this,’ Tuchel said after announcing his latest England squad on Friday.

‘We could understand the disappointment of the fans with what happened before but I think this is expressed now and this should be a closed book because I think everyone could also see the investment of Ben, the quality of Ben and how he presented himself in the March camp before the World Cup.

‘He did excellent, scored for us and then I think he committed a foul and we conceded. It was very eventful, not so easy to come back. When I speak to him, I always feel the hunger to come back, the excitement. He missed the last camp.

#1822. Besiktas vs Genclerbirligi - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:57, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 20:53

Besiktas will look to return to winning ways when they welcome Genclerbirligi to Tupras Stadium on Sunday in the Turkish Super Lig.

The Black Eagles sit fourth in the standings with 19 points from their opening 10 matches, while the visitors occupy 14th place with 11 points after an inconsistent start to their return to the top flight.

Besiktas have made a reasonably encouraging start to the campaign but will be frustrated by their inability to maintain consistency, having collected just seven points from their last five league matches (W2, D1, L2).

Vincenzo Italiano's side were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa in their most recent league outing, despite taking the lead twice, following a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir that had provided a timely response to their 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

They have also struggled to find consistent success in Europe, drawing 2-2 with Crystal Palace before suffering a disappointing 3-2 defeat away to Celtic in the Europa League on Thursday, leaving them with just one win from their three matches in the competition, a 3-2 victory over Hoffenheim.

Nevertheless, their home form should provide encouragement heading into this clash, having won all five of their league matches at Tupras Stadium this season and remained unbeaten there across all competitions.

However, the hosts will be hoping to buck the recent trend in this fixture, with the away side winning each of the last five competitive meetings between the teams.

Genclerbirligi, meanwhile, head to Istanbul with renewed confidence after producing one of their best performances of the season in a 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor.

Bernd Storck's side ended a seven-game winless run in the league with that result (D2, L5), which also followed a 5-0 victory over Karakopru in the Turkish Cup, giving them momentum ahead of Sunday's encounter.

The visitors will hope to carry that confidence into their next away fixture as they look to end a three-game losing run on the road, during which they have conceded 11 goals without scoring.

Their only away victory and goal of the campaign coming against Goztepe (1-0) in their opening trip, with no side scoring fewer than them on the road in this campaign.

Besiktas are expected to remain without Fabio Miretti, who is sidelined with a shoulder problem, while Umit Akdag is also set to miss out with a broken wrist and Milot Rashica continues his recovery from a hamstring injury.

Dusan Vlahovic should lead the attack after scoring seven league goals this season, with Leandro Trossard and Vaclav Cerny likely to provide support in the final third.

Orkun Kokcu returned from injury against Celtic and marked his comeback with a goal, putting himself in contention to start in midfield alongside Junior Olaitan and Salih Ozcan.

Genclerbirligi also have several availability concerns, with Dimitrios Goutas facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering a cruciate ligament injury.

Pedro Pereira and Kevin Rodrigues are also carrying fitness problems, while Peter Etebo remains a doubt with a muscle injury.

Franco Tongya will be one to watch for the visitors after scoring twice in the league this season, while Tiago Gouveia and Adama Traore are expected to provide attacking support after featuring in the 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor.

Nubel; Murillo, Agbadou, Topcu, Ouattara; Ozcan; Cerny, Kokcu, Olaitan, Trossard; Vlahovic

Egribayat; Celik, Baltaci, Thalisson, Aydar; Niasse; Gouveia, Ulgun, Tongya, Traore; Mendes

Genclerbirligi's recent victories mean they should arrive in Istanbul with renewed confidence, but reproducing their attacking performance against Besiktas will be considerably more difficult.

The visitors' poor away record is another concern, and we expect the hosts to have too much quality at Tupras Stadium as they return to winning ways with a comfortable victory.

#1820. Arsenal told why Antonio Nusa will join them in £50m January transfer

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have been told they lead the race for Antonio Nusa ahead of a £50million January transfer battle for the RB Leipzig winger.

The Gunners are expected to make attempts to improve their attack in the upcoming mid-season transfer window, in light of their struggles up front, and Nusa has been heavily linked in recent days.

The 21-year-old Norway international has attracted interest after an impressive start to the season which has seen him score six goals and provide seven assists in 13 Bundesliga appearances.

Nusa is less experienced then other reported Arsenal targets, such as Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi and Juventus wonderkid Kenan Yildiz, but could been more attainable in January.

Former Norway midfielder Kristoffer Lokberg believes Nusa is now ready to make another step in his career and says Arsenal are the strongest option.

Speaking on NRK's Bakrommet podcast, via Sport Witness, he said: “He is one of the world’s most exciting left-wingers. We have been waiting for his potential to come to full bloom, but now it is exploding.

“Big clubs can no longer sit on the fence, they must act quickly before he disappears, or they will be left regretting it.”

Leipzig are reportedly demanding at least £50m for Nusa, though Lokberg believes a figure closer to £40m could force the club’s hand.

Lokberg continued: “The completely obvious option in the Premier League is Arsenal.

“The player fits their playing style, and the club has a real need. They basically only have Tzolis and a slightly half-hearted Eberechi Eze as options on the left wing. I think Arsenal sit around every day, weighing whether to pull the trigger.”

#1819. JJ Gabriel reveals key motivation behind Real Madrid transfer after Man Utd exit

JJ Gabriel has revealed the key motivation behind his impending move to Real Madrid after turning his back on Manchester United.

Gabriel, who turned 16 on October 6, informed United of his desire to leave in September and has not trained with the club since then.

The young forward has attracted interest from several clubs across Europe, but has now reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

The forward joined United’s academy four years ago and quickly established himself as one of the most highly-rated youngsters at the club, featuring for the U18 side at the age of just 14.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Gabriel played under Michael Carrick during the club’s pre-season camp, but his entourage are understood to have grown unhappy with his first-team integration and playing opportunities at United.

The teenager, who has an Irish passport, could finalise a move to the Spanish giants as early as January next year, with United reportedly set to receive £350,000 in compensation.

And in a brief interview with the Spanish outlet Marca, Gabriel revealed he has one particular goal in mind for his time at Real.

‘My dream is to win a Ballon d’Or,’ he said.

When asked about a potential move to Barcelona instead, Gabriel simply responded: ‘Obviously, Madrid.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

A move to Real is a bold step at such a young age, and United legend Ryan Giggs believes Gabriel may have been better served following the example of Max Dowman, whose development is not being rushed by Arsenal or Mikel Arteta.

📰🔜 JJ Gabriel with Marca’s front page confirming the move to Real Madrid is close: “Can I keep this [newspaper] with me?”. pic.twitter.com/cerdxXsbE4

‘So far in his career everything is going fine, why would you disrupt that? You’re on the right track,’ Giggs said of Gabriel on Rio Ferdinand Presents.

‘I trained at 15, I didn’t play for the first team until two years later so you have to have that patience that people just don’t seem to have at the moment.

‘And believe it or not, first-team football for Man United is completely different to playing in the youth team, playing pre-season for the first team, it’s completely different. That first game, yeah, you might do alright, but you have to do it for 40, 50 games a season. You’re going to get injuries, loss of form, bad results, so you have to be patient.

‘If you’re on the right trajectory then just bide your time, no matter how good you are.

‘Max Dowman is unbelievable but he’s not playing for Arsenal at the moment.

‘I’m sure he’ll bide his time, I’m sure he’s getting impatient, but he’s not kicking off, he knows in a couple of years time he might be the main man for Arsenal.’

#1818. Villarreal vs Getafe - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 18:58, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 19:00

Villarreal will be bidding to bounce back from a heavy European defeat when they continue their La Liga campaign against Getafe on Sunday.

The Yellow Submarine suffered a 6-0 loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last time out, while Getafe were beaten 1-0 by Brighton & Hove Albion in the Conference League.

Villarreal suffered a surprise 1-0 home defeat to Espanyol in Spain's top flight last weekend, before conceding six unanswered goals against PSG in Europe on Tuesday, so there is pressure on the Yellow Submarine to issue a response here.

Inigo Perez's side are currently ninth in the La Liga table, boasting a record of three wins, three draws and five defeats from 11 matches, which has seen them collect 12 points.

Villarreal finished third in Spain's top flight last season, but they have had their issues domestically this term, and another top-four finish might be beyond them this term.

The Yellow Submarine have only won one of their last four in the league, and they have actually only been victorious in one of their five home La Liga matches this season.

Villarreal have won 27 of their previous 49 matches against Getafe, but it was 2-1 to the latter when the two teams last locked horns in February of this year.

Getafe's success over Villarreal in February 2026 actually proved to be their first victory against the Yellow Submarine of any kind since January 2019.

The capital outfit have only beaten the Yellow Submarine on 10 previous occasions throughout history, and they will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 loss to Brighton in the Conference League.

That said, Jose Bordalas' side have been victorious in two of their last three matches, including a 3-1 success over Sevilla in their last league game.

Getafe have won three, drawn three and lost five of their 11 league games this season - the same record as Villarreal - with 12 points leaving them 13th in the table.

Finding the back of the net has been a major issue for the capital outfit this term, having only netted eight goals, which is the joint-worst attacking record in the division.

Villarreal will be without the services of Alassane Diatta for a lengthy period due to a severe hamstring injury, while Gerard Moreno, Juan Foyth and Ilias Akhomach are all regarded as fitness doubts at this stage of proceedings.

However, Pape Gueye has served his suspension and will return to the squad, while Nathan Saliba is available again after a knock.

There will be changes to the side that took to the field for the first whistle against PSG, with Alberto Moleiro, Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona among those expected to start.

Getafe, meanwhile, remain without long-term absentee Christantus Uche; Juanmi and Zaid Romero are also regarded as doubts for this contest.

Enes Unal has netted twice in 10 league appearances this season and is set to return in the final third of the field this weekend.

There will also be a return at right-back for Dani Carvajal following the team's European contest with Brighton on Thursday night.

Gulacsi; Freeman, Navarro, Veiga, Cardona; Gueye, Comesana; Pepe, Moleiro, Buchanan; Mikautadze

Soria; Carvajal, Dakonam, Boselli, Mojica; Garcia, Mangala, Gudelj, Terrats; Satriano, Unal

Villarreal will have had longer to prepare for this match due to Getafe's European commitments on Thursday, and we are expecting the Yellow Submarine to navigate their way to all three points.

#1817. ‘Great signing’ – Liverpool urged to make stunning transfer bid for £29m Chelsea star

Emile Heskey has urged his former side Liverpool to pursue the audacious signing of young Chelsea forward Estevao.

Estevao was a bright spark against Manchester United last weekend in what was his first Premier League start of the season.

But outside of that display, the Brazilian has struggled for game time so far this season under Xabi Alonso, with the form of other attackers limiting him to just 134 minutes of playing time in the league.

Reports earlier in the season claimed that the 19-year-old had become frustrated over his lack of playing opportunities under his new boss.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

And while Alonso has insisted that Estevao has a bright future ahead of him at Chelsea, Heskey wonders if Liverpool could lure the Brazilian to Anfield with the promise of more regular starts.

‘Estevao would be a great signing for Liverpool,’ he told Eldorado.

‘You look at what he would bring, his drive on the ball and everything, he’s a very tidy player, and that is exactly what Liverpool still miss after losing Mohamed Salah, someone who is more direct.

‘It would put pressure on the other wingers who are great players as well but it ups the ante, and he’d love the chance to get more chances to show what he can do because he’s been out of the reckoning at times for someone of his talent.’

Speaking before Estevao’s start against United last weekend, Alonso insisted that there were no plans for the Brazilian to leave the club on loan in the January transfer window.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘No discussions about that,’ Alonso said.

‘It’s no secret that all players want to be on the pitch. When any of them haven’t had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that.

‘But everyone has to be ready because in any game they could be important. Este, his training and his attitude has been good.’

But former Liverpool captain believes that Estevao could soon prove to be a selection headache for Alonso, particularly when Joao Pedro returns from injury after the international break.

‘He’s exciting. He’s great to watch,’ Gerrard said on The Overlap.

‘Your typical Brazilian, where it’s about flair, it’s about quality, but I really like that he’s very direct. I like that he’s hungry to get shots off.

‘So, he’s desperate to impress the manager. And he’s going to give Xabi a problem when Joao Pedro comes back, because Pedro Neto’s a great player as well, but five doesn’t go into that front four, so it’s going to be interesting.’

#1816. When is FA Cup draw? Date, start time, second round ball numbers and TV channel

The FA Cup continues apace this weekend with the draw for the second round.

League One and League Two clubs have joined the action, with one of the pick of the ties seeing Robbie Savage facing off against his son, Charlie, as Peterborough host Reading.

The FA Cup first round ties began on Friday night with 2021 winners Leicester seeing off Oxford City. Elsewhere, 2013 winners Wigan are aiming to avoid an early exit at the hands of Boreham Wood.

Eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds and Stafford Rangers - the lowest-ranked teams remaining in the competition - face off against Burton Albion and Grimsby Town respectively, raising the prospect of a major giant-killing.

The weekend’s action will see 80 teams whittled down to 40 for the second round, with Championship and Premier League teams entering the fray in the third round.

Here’s everything you need to know about the FA Cup draw for the second round...

The draw for the FA Cup second round will take place on Monday, November 9, 2026, before the clash between non-league clubs Plymouth Parkway and Berkhamsted.

Television coverage of the game starts at 6:30pm GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live on TNT Sports 1.

Live blog: You can follow all draw via Standard Sport’s live blog.

The ball numbers are to be confirmed closer to the second round draw.

Kidderminster Harriers vs Doncaster Rovers

The second round ties will be played across the weekend of December 5-6, 2026.

#1815. Neil Warnock says Man Utd should have signed Ezri Konsa before Arsenal

Former Premier League manager Neil Warnock believes Manchester United should have looked to sign Ezri Konsa before his £55million move to Arsenal.

Konsa has enjoyed a brilliant start to his Gunners career following a big-money move from Aston Villa over the summer.

The 29-year-old came straight into Mikel Arteta’s team due to William Saliba’s injury lay-off and has helped Arsenal win eight of their first nine Premier League matches so far this season.

Conversely, it has been a miserable start to the season for United, who have not tasted victory in the league since a 5-2 win over Ipswich Town in late August.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

That start has seen United’s recruitment strategy placed under the microscope, most notably their failure to address a glaring lack of depth in defence in the summer transfer window.

And Warnock cited Konsa’s move to Arsenal as one deal that United should have looked to pursue instead of their all-out focus on signing midfielders.

‘They spend money on forwards, they spend money on midfield players like you’ve never seen and yet they still haven’t got a defence,’ Warnock told The Mirror.

‘I don’t understand how a top club like that can’t buy defenders – and they’ve never had any full backs that can defend either.

‘They could have bought Konsa this year. Why didn’t they spend money like that? They’d rather spent £100million on a midfielder – even though the defenders can’t defend!’

Warnock continued: ‘If nothing changes, they are going to struggle. I’m not bothered who comes in. They will struggle.

‘You look at Brighton and Bournemouth and clubs like that, and you think that’s a good [recruitment strategy]… But when you look at Man United, if the recruitment can’t see that what I’ve seen for the last five years, there’s something wrong somewhere.’
